content.overview: CPUs and compilers reorder memory operations. A barrier constrains reordering so effects become visible to other cores in algorithm-required order. Barriers order existing traffic; they do not flush caches or serialize execution.

taxonomy.name: smp_wmb
taxonomy.effect: stores before are visible before stores after

taxonomy.name: smp_rmb
taxonomy.effect: loads before complete before loads after

taxonomy.name: smp_mb
taxonomy.effect: orders loads and stores across the point

taxonomy.name: acquire
taxonomy.effect: no op after moves before it; pairs with release

taxonomy.name: release
taxonomy.effect: no op before moves after it; pairs with acquire

required_patterns.rule: writer: store payload, release-store flag. reader: acquire-load flag, then load payload. Without the pair, reader can see flag set with stale payload.
wmb before in-counter publish; rmb before out-counter publish (see systems.concurrency.ring_buffer)
broken without acquire on pointer load

invariants: barriers are pairwise: writer-side ordering is meaningless without reader-side pairing
on x86 TSO most read barriers compile to nothing, but the compiler barrier remains mandatory
relaxed atomics synchronize nothing by themselves
